content:
A moving coil galvanometer has resistance 50<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.633ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -704 722 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="3A9" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-3A9"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>
and it indicates full deflection at 4mA current.
A voltmeter is made using this galvanometer
and a 5 k<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.633ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -704 722 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="3A9" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-3A9"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> resistance. The maximum voltage,
that can be measured using this voltmeter, will
be close to :
explanation:
G = 50

S = 5000

Ig = 4 × 10–3

V = ig (G + S)

V = 4 × 10–3 (50 + 5000)

= 4 × 10–3 (5050) = 20.2 volt
